chunks: I would wish that I had a thousand horsemen from among you, of the Banu Firas ibn Ghanm: there, if you called them, they would come to you like the shooting of the summer cloud.

key_terms.أَرْمِيَةُ الْحَمِيمِ: the shooting of the summer cloud, a poetic metaphor for rapid and abundant arrival
key_terms.بَنِي فِرَاسِ بْنِ غَنْمَ: Banu Firas ibn Ghanm, a prominent Arab tribe known for military prowess

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'armiyat al-hamim' mean in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) expresses his desire for a thousand elite horsemen from the Banu Firas ibn Ghanm tribe, using a poetic simile of 'the shooting of the summer cloud' (armiyat al-hamim) to describe their swift and abundant arrival when called. This reference highlights the renowned martial prowess of this specific tribe, known for their speed and agility in battle, which Ali viewed as the ideal military force to counter the strategic maneuvers of Muawiya. The quote underscores Ali’s pragmatic assessment of tribal strengths during the period of political tension and impending conflict with the Umayyads.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I wish I had only a thousand horsemen of Banu Firās ibn Ghanm (as the poet says) : If you call them the horsemen would come to you like the summer cloud.
